transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2028-08-09 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~55m
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Elena (Redwood SE), Jasper (Redwood), Maya (AuroraEdge VP Eng), Rajat (AuroraEdge SRE), Priya (AuroraEdge CTO), Leo (AuroraEdge Platform)

Summary: Quick postmortem of last week's lab runs; focus on 95th pctl latency delta vs incumbent, small-window throughput anomalies at high concurrency, and next-step gating items (dedicated slot, traces, security check).
Topics: benchmark artifacts, 95th vs p50/p90 divergence, KV cache priming, batch sizing, quantized model runs, routing fallback under load, cost delta at token-level.

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining. we planned a tighter 55 min, so we'll go through the head-to-head results then next steps. Elena, you want to kick off with the top-line?
[00:12] Elena: yeah for sure. ok, we compared Redwood's inference runtime against AuroraEdge's incumbent provider using the test harness you gave us. test parameters were: 1k warmup requests, 10k sample, payloads avg token length ~220, concurrency sweeps 1-64. we ran both quantized and fp16 variants.
[00:34] Maya: sounds right. couple clarifications: the incumbent used a 2x gpu pool and their batching was 32 by default, right?
[00:40] Elena: right, they used batch=32, we tested Redwood at batch=16, 32 and 48 to match and to tune.
[00:52] Rajat: ya we should highlight that our baseline's 95th is artificially low because they have aggressive response buffering upstream — which masks tail latencies.
[01:03] Jasper: note, that buffering you mentioned often shows as lower p95 but increases end-to-end system latency if you include network aggregator time. our numbers are model-side only.
[01:13] Priya: ok show us the numbers then.

[01:18] Elena: top-line: median latency (p50) across typical prompts: Redwood fp16 = 42ms, incumbent fp16 = 48ms. p90: Redwood 78ms vs incumbent 86ms. p95: Redwood 142ms vs incumbent 118ms — so we saw a tail regression there on Redwood in one of the high-concurrency runs. throughput at steady-state (concurrency 32): Redwood sustained 260 reqs/s, incumbent 290 reqs/s.
[01:48] Samir: important to call out that the p95 regression happened during a bursty traffic pattern where our KV cache wasn't fully primed and we observed 2-3x variance at key-switches.
[01:59] Rajat: can you explain the KV cache priming behavior? we saw a couple of outliers at ~400ms.
[02:06] Elena: sure, so when the request sequence includes many unique prefixes the KV cache can't reuse kv entries, so attention recomputation hits. in our lab the cache warmed up after ~300 requests, but in the short-burst tests the priming lag caused a few 350-420ms outliers in p99 land.
[02:22] Leo: those numbers track with what we saw. on our side the incumbent's buffering smoothed those outliers, which made their p95 look better but introduced more end-to-end jitter.
[02:34] Jasper: one more thing — we also tested Redwood with prefix caching enabled across consecutive sessions (persisted KV between requests) and p95 dropped to 98ms, throughput modestly up to 310 rps at concurrency 32. so caching strategy matters a ton.

[02:50] Maya: interesting, did you run the quantized run? our infra team was worried about accuracy regressions with QAT quant.
[02:58] Elena: yes, we ran 8-bit quant with QAT profiles you suggested. median was ~48ms, p95 ~130ms; throughput at concurrency 32 was 305 rps. quality delta was within your eval set tolerance (ROUGE/drop <0.2%).
[03:17] Priya: good. cost-wise how does that compare?
[03:20] Samir: at token-level unit economics using our recommended batching and cache, the cost per 1k tokens is ~18% lower than the incumbent for the quantized profile; fp16 runs were within 5% cost parity. We'll share the cost ladder.

[03:34] Rajat: you mentioned one-off anomalies in throughput — can you point to root cause? we saw a couple of 10-15% dips at minute marks.
[03:45] Elena: yes that was scheduling jitter tied to host GC spikes in our test harness containerization layer — we traced a small CPU spike that impacted dispatcher thread during high concurrency bursts. we have a fix in PR that pins the dispatcher and reduces jitter.
[03:58] Samir: also worthy of note: when we routed traffic across regions, the cross-region RT increases made a big difference. so routing policy for production will matter (we recommend region pinning for latency-sensitive endpoints).

[04:12] Maya: on dedicated vs hosted: if we choose Dedicated, do you guarantee those tail latencies? our SLA needs a 95th <120ms.
[04:21] Samir: Dedicated gives you much tighter isolation and predictable throughput; with Dedicated + prefix cache warmup and batch tuning we can meet p95 <120ms consistently. we'll propose a dedicated slot for a 24h head-to-head to validate.
[04:32] Priya: ok if we can validate that in-scope, that's compelling.

[04:38] Elena: quick demo of a specific run (screen share paraphrase): at 32 concurrency with persisted KV and quant profile — we saw p50 40ms, p90 72ms, p95 97ms, throughput 320 rps. Without persisted KV, p95 jumped to 140ms.
[04:58] Rajat: that's a big swing. is persisted KV something we can control on customer side? does it have storage or security implications?
[05:06] Jasper: it's part of the serving runtime, we persist KV to ephemeral encrypted memory within the host. nothing written to disk by default. for private deployments we can integrate with your KMS for key rotation — there's an audit trail.
[05:18] Priya: we need details for compliance; encryption-at-rest and audit logs are musts.
[05:22] Samir: noted — security follow-up is a next-step.

[05:27] Leo: one question — how deterministic are your throughput numbers vs different sequence distributions? our sequences vary a lot (short prompts vs long).
[05:35] Elena: we ran synthetic mixes: 30% short, 50% medium (200 tokens), 20% long (1k tokens). throughput scaled roughly linearly; tail latencies increased when long-request proportion hit >25%. we can provide the raw traces so you can re-run with your exact traffic model.

[05:55] Maya: about routing fallback — in our incident model we want automatic fallback to a cheaper model when latency SLOs breach. do you offer that?
[06:02] Samir: yes that's the smart routing feature — you can configure policy-based fallback (latency, cost, region). we can demo a canary rule that falls back to a smaller quantized model if p95 crosses threshold for >5s.

[06:12] Rajat: how does that affect consistency? we can't have the model change responses silently to prod users.
[06:18] Jasper: you can tie fallback to a header/route and flag. also our rollout system can run shadow compare and only switch after N successful shadow comparisons. you can also log model variant in response headers for auditing.

[06:35] Elena: quick note on batching: for your workload we recommend dynamic batching up to 48 for throughput-oriented endpoints and lower batch sizes for low-latency endpoints. dynamic batching thresholds are tunable in the Console.

[06:48] Maya: one operational ask: we'd like a reproducible test harness — can you share the exact script and docker images?
[06:53] Samir: yes we'll provide the harness, the docker image ref and the terraform to spin up the ephemeral infra.

[07:00] [07:00 - 24:00] -- LAB DATA WALKTHROUGH -- Samir/Elena narrate specific rows from the benchmark sheet: run ids, seed prompts, p50/p90/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization at sample points, cache hit-rates, network RTT. occasional interruptions and clarifying questions from Rajat.

[24:05] Rajat: looking at run 27, I see a couple of p99 spikes around 420ms — what's the stack trace?
[24:12] Elena: those align with dispatcher reschedule events and a couple of model-mmap misses when we loaded a new quant kernel. the fix is to preload kernels and pin pages; that reduces those misses.

[24:30] Maya: on the cost sheet, it looks like quantized runs shift cost to compute vs memory. can you elaborate?
[24:38] Samir: sure, quant reduces memory bandwidth and cache pressure so you can fit larger batch sizes which improves amortized GPU overhead; compute-efficiency gains offset increased per-token compute in some cases. overall unit-cost improves for most of your mixes.

[24:55] Priya: any visibility into how this would work with our private (VPC) deployment?
[24:59] Jasper: private VPC deployment supports the same runtime and caching behavior, with customer-managed networking. KMS/HSM integration is supported for keys; audit logs are exportable to your SIEM. we can include an on-prem agent if needed.

[25:12] Leo: we are particularly worried about tail behavior during batch-surge events. is there a mitigation playbook?
[25:18] Elena: yes mitigation steps: 1) persistent KV priming across sessions; 2) route burst traffic to dedicated pool; 3) configure fallback to smaller model; 4) tune dispatcher pinning. We'll share a written playbook.

[25:30] Maya: ok let's be pragmatic. we want a 2-hour head-to-head with dedicated slot, run your suggested playbook, and replicate our real traffic mix. If p95 <120ms then we proceed to security and contract discussions.

[25:42] Samir: sounds fair. proposed timeline: we provision dedicated slot week of 8/14, run 24h dark-launch and a 2h focused head-to-head test, share raw traces and consolidated CSV, then security meeting.

[25:53] Rajat: scheduling note — we'll need the results before our exec review on 8/23.

[26:00] Elena: action items recap, I'll put the exact run ids in the sheet and annotate the kernel preload patch.
[26:05] Samir: i'll send the cost ladder and a short one-pager on routing fallbacks.
[26:09] Maya: i'll confirm which endpoints are in-scope for the head-to-head and our exact traffic mix.

[26:15] [Q&A volley] - small clarifications about instrumentation, span correlation ids, and whether Redwood can push traces into AuroraEdge's Jaeger instance. Jasper confirms trace exporters are supported.

[32:02] Rajat: last item — we noticed the incumbent had slightly better sustained throughput in one configuration (290 rps vs your 260 rps) — do you think you can close that gap?
[32:12] Elena: yes after kernel-preload, dispatcher pinning, and persisted KV our steady-state throughput was 310 rps in quant mode. we'll reproduce that in the dedicated run.

[32:25] Priya: any legal or procurement blockers we should be aware of?
[32:29] Samir: we'll surface standard terms; for Private deployments we can provide a SOC2 package and enterprise addendum. Security follow-up will cover KMS/HSM and audit logs.

[32:40] Maya: ok next steps recap?
[32:44] Samir: recap: 1) Samir shares p95 traces and CSV by 8/12; 2) Elena provisions dedicated slot and test harness by 8/14; 3) AuroraEdge runs dark-launch 24h and focused 2h head-to-head week of 8/14 and posts results by 8/15; 4) security sync for KMS/HSM 8/16 tentatively.

[32:59] Maya: thanks, that covers it. any other quick questions?
[33:05] Rajat: no, thanks.
[33:07] Samir: great, we'll follow up in email with meeting notes and artifacts. thanks everyone.

Meeting end: 15:55 UTC

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-heard proper nouns (KV cache → KV cash in one snippet), and timestamps approximate. The exported sheet links: (benchmark-sheet.xlsx) and (traces/ff-20280809-auroraedge-runs.zip) were referenced in-chat.
